items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-06-20
items.q: Mr. Dillon, are you referring to my office? I want to bring you before the board for that. ... But you know what? They brought me before the board.

ctx.x: So the unions were pretty strict, wherever you played, they would check?

Yeah, they would check, you know. And more hassle, you know, than anything. That right to work wasn't so much enforced then like it is now. Because the union don't even bother you no more. They leave it up to you to take care. See like last Friday night I played at the Royal Lawley bourbon all the time. And I paid them yesterday. They don't bother me no more because I'm going to pay them, but I'm going to cheat them too first year every time I get. And I guess they know that. Because the union, our union really…
